speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling
text: asked the Minister for Manpower to what extent should an employer be made responsible for a migrant domestic worker's medical fee in Singapore if the treatment needed is a consequence of the worker's own social activity during her personal off-time and on her own free will and the medical fee quantum far exceeds the insurance limits.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad) (for the Minister for Manpower)
text: Employers may repatriate their MDWs after their MDWs are certified fit for discharge and/or fit for flight.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad) (for the Minister for Manpower)
text: Beyond the mandated coverage, employers can opt for higher coverage from their insurers to better protect themselves against large bills.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad) (for the Minister for Manpower)
text: Employers who face financial difficulties in paying for their MDWs' medical bills can also approach medical social workers at the hospitals for assistance.

speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (MacPherson)
text: I ask this question because I have a resident who is probably one of a very few cases whereby the MDW was diagnosed with several sexually transmitted diseases (STDs) and it was discovered only on her way to the airport to take a flight back home.

speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (MacPherson)
text: The work permit at that point would have been terminated.

speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (MacPherson)
text: The employer who was an elderly was expected to be responsible for the bill.

speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (MacPherson)
text: I think under normal circumstances, if the illness or accidents, even if it is not work-related, is of no fault of the MDW, I think it would have been reasonable.

speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (MacPherson)
text: But in this case, it seemed to be an excessive burden on the employer.

speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (MacPherson)
text: To be fair, MOM and the hospital did try to come in to provide assistance.

speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (MacPherson)
text: But my question is, is it equitable in such instances, albeit rare, for the employer to take up such a responsibility?

speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (MacPherson)
text: Should the responsibility, therefore, be shared by the MDW?

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: Indeed, I can fully understand the challenges that she faced and perhaps that feeling that it was not equitable, that this was not the fault of the employer.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: I recognise that employers generally depend on their Migrant Domestic Workers for a variety of reasons, whether it is help for cleaning, whether it is caregiving for the elders or children.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: When we employ a Migrant Domestic Worker, one thing we have to note is that we are not just hiring an employee.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: We are also having a person, a human.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: So, there is a benefit that we get from the work; there is also the risk of indiscretion, just like any humans, just like us.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: We understand that due to the MDW's varying financial situations, we know that they are paid above several hundred dollars a month.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: Therefore, in terms of affordability, it is certainly very difficult.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: Therefore, we also have a medical insurance scheme today.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: This medical insurance scheme covers up to 95% of most medical bills.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: Minister Tan See Leng shared in a Parliamentary Question earlier this year, that hospitals administer on our behalf, to help the outlier cases, such as this.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: Rest assured, whether they are work-related or not work-related, we will try to help employers as much as we can.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: But, ultimately, it is a fine balance that we are trying to also achieve.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: But at the same time, in cases like this, rest assured we will do our best to help your resident.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: I will take the case up separately with you offline.
